headline: Treasure Coast traffic report: I-95 ramp closures, road work planned Oct. 3-9
teaser: Overnight I-95 ramp closures in Martin and St. Lucie counties, extended neighborhood road closures in Port St. Lucie and lane restrictions across the Treasure Coast are planned for Oct. 3-9.
body:
Drivers across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties should expect overnight interstate work, ramp closures, neighborhood road closures and daytime lane restrictions during the coming week, according to the Florida Department of Transportation's Treasure Coast traffic report.

The most significant disruptions include three I-95 ramp closures in Martin County, an I-95 exit closure at Becker Road in Port St. Lucie, extended closures on several roads off SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and weekend work at the Sebastian River High School entrance.

FDOT schedules can change because of weather or other conditions. Drivers can check [FL511](https://www.fl511.com/) for real-time interstate traffic information.

## Biggest closures to know about

- **I-95 southbound exit ramp to C.R. 713/SW High Meadow Avenue, Exit 102:** Closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, through Thursday, Oct. 8, for wrong-way vehicle testing. Drivers will be detoured south on I-95 to the **S.R. 76/SW Kanner Highway exit, Exit 101**, then east on Kanner Highway and back north on I-95 to Exit 102. FDOT says only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

- **I-95 southbound exit ramp to C.R. 708/SE Bridge Road, Exit 96:** Closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, through Thursday, Oct. 8, for wrong-way vehicle testing. The detour uses the **S.R. 76/SW Kanner Highway exit**, **C.R. 711/Pratt-Whitney Road** and **C.R. 708/SE Bridge Road**.

- **I-95 northbound entrance ramp from C.R. 713/SW High Meadow Avenue:** Closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, through Thursday, Oct. 8, for milling and resurfacing. Drivers will be directed south on I-95 to the **S.R. 76/SW Kanner Highway exit** and then back to the northbound entrance.

- **I-95 southbound exit ramp to SW Becker Road, Exit 114:** Closed from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, through Thursday, Oct. 8, for milling and resurfacing. The detour uses **SW Tradition Parkway/SW Gatlin Boulevard, Exit 118**, **Village Parkway** and **SW Becker Road**.

- **SW Koler Avenue between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Kober Road:** Extended closures may begin Monday, Oct. 5, and continue through Friday, Oct. 9, while crews install drainage and utilities.

- **SW McCall Road between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Kabane Street:** Extended closures may occur Monday through Friday as part of the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

- **SW McCoy Avenue between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Jamros Street:** Extended closures may occur Monday through Friday for drainage and utility work.

- **SW Paar Drive between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW McCandless Street, and between SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard and SW Jaqust Street:** Eastbound and westbound closures may occur during the week. Access to homes and businesses will be maintained, and adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time.

- **S.R. 510/90th Avenue at Sebastian River High School and the Hammerhead Way entrance:** The southbound entrance area will be closed from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 3, and Sunday, Oct. 4, for repaving. Access to Sebastian River High School will remain available.

FDOT says the overnight work is scheduled to continue through Nov. 24 for signage, milling and resurfacing.

- **S.R. A1A/NE Ocean Boulevard from NE Shore Village Terrace to south of the S.R. 732/Jensen Beach Causeway:** One lane will close intermittently Monday, Oct. 5, through Friday, Oct. 9, for pavement widening and drainage work. Two-way traffic will be maintained with flaggers.

headline: St. Lucie County changes polling location for Precincts 39 and 52 for Nov. 3 election
teaser: Voters in Precincts 39 and 52 will cast Election Day ballots at Lakewood Park Church instead of Spanish Lakes Country Club because of clubhouse renovations.
body:
Voters in St. Lucie County Precincts 39 and 52 will have a temporary polling place for the Nov. 3 general election because of renovations at their usual Election Day location.

The two precincts will move from the Spanish Lakes Country Club clubhouse to **Lakewood Park Church, 5405 Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce**, according to St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker. The change applies to the Nov. 3, 2026 General Election.

Walker encouraged voters to consider early voting, including the county's newest early voting site at Lakewood Park Branch Library, to help avoid Election Day lines.

## Early voting runs Oct. 19 through Oct. 31

Early voting will be available from **10 a.m. to 6 p.m. each day from Oct. 19 through Oct. 31** at eight locations across St. Lucie County:

- **Lakewood Park Branch Library:** 7605 Santa Barbara Drive, Fort Pierce
- **Renaissance Business Park, Main Office:** 4132 Okeechobee Road, Fort Pierce
- **Zora Neale Hurston Library:** 3008 Avenue D, Fort Pierce
- **MIDFlorida Credit Union Event Center:** 9221 SE Event Center Place, Port St. Lucie
- **Port St. Lucie Community Center:** 2195 SE Airoso Boulevard, Port St. Lucie
- **Paula A. Lewis Library:** 2950 Rosser Boulevard, Port St. Lucie
- **Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence:** 500 NW California Boulevard, Port St. Lucie
- **Robert E. Minsky Gym:** 750 SW Darwin Boulevard, Port St. Lucie

## Vote-by-mail deadline is Oct. 22

St. Lucie County voters may request a vote-by-mail ballot through **Oct. 22**. The Supervisor of Elections office recommends returning ballots by mail at least seven days before Election Day.

Voters may also return vote-by-mail ballots at an early voting site or at one of the following Supervisor of Elections locations:

- **Renaissance Business Park, Main Office:** 4132 Okeechobee Road, Fort Pierce
- **St. Lucie West South County Annex:** 250 NW Country Club Drive, Port St. Lucie
- **Dorothy J. Conrad Administration Annex:** 1664 SE Walton Road, Port St. Lucie
- **Tradition Tax Collector:** 10264 SW Village Parkway, Port St. Lucie

More election information, including instructions for requesting a vote-by-mail ballot, is available at [StLucieVotes.gov](https://www.stlucievotes.gov/). Voters may also contact the St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections office at **772-462-1500**.
source_headline: Temporary Polling Place Changes for Precincts 39 and 52 for November 3, 2026 General Election

headline: Three generations later, Packard Roofing remains rooted on the Treasure Coast
teaser: Founded in Miami in 1971 and established on the Treasure Coast in 1994, Packard Roofing & Waterproofing is now led by third-generation siblings Brian Packard and Stephanie Packard Smith.
body:
For the Packard family, roofing has never been simply a business passed from one generation to the next. It has been a trade learned firsthand, a family responsibility and, over time, a connection to the communities the company serves.

[Packard Roofing & Waterproofing](https://www.packardroofing.com/) has grown from a South Florida roofing company into a multigenerational operation serving homeowners across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

The Port St. Lucie family business was founded in Miami in 1971 by Raymond M. Packard and David R. Packard. More than two decades later, the company expanded to Port St. Lucie in 1994, establishing the Treasure Coast operation that now serves customers across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

Today, the company is led by third-generation siblings Brian Packard and Stephanie Packard Smith.

Brian's path into the family business started well before he was old enough to run one. As a teenager, he spent summers cleaning and organizing the warehouse and service yard. Later came tear-off crews, repair work, and eventually handling residential and commercial projects himself.

Stephanie's history with the company also stretches back decades. She joined during the hectic aftermath of Hurricane Andrew in 1992, when South Florida roofing companies were dealing with enormous demand while Packard Roofing was also recovering from storm damage to its own facilities. She went on to become a central part of the company's office operations.

Brian relocated from Miami to Port St. Lucie in 2021 as the family prepared for another transition. Following their father David Packard's death in 2022, Brian and Stephanie took responsibility for leading the company into its third generation.

## A business built around the Treasure Coast

Packard Roofing's headquarters at 2182 NW Reserve Park Trace places the company beside PGA Village in Port St. Lucie, with much of its work concentrated throughout the Treasure Coast.

The company handles roof repairs, roof replacements, new roof construction, and maintenance for homeowners throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

That local focus matters in a region where roofs face intense sun, heavy rainfall, tropical weather, and wind-driven rain. For homeowners, problems can range from persistent leaks and storm damage to aging roofs that have reached the end of their useful lifespan.

[Packard Roofing's website](https://www.packardroofing.com/) also provides homeowners with information about issues such as hurricane preparation, wind damage, roof leaks, and deciding when a roof should be repaired rather than replaced.

For a company with decades behind it, that focus reflects an effort to remain useful to homeowners before they ever need a major roofing project.

## Experience that stayed with the company

The Packard family is not the only long-term presence in the business.

Superintendent Mark Hanna has worked with the company for more than 30 years, beginning as a repairman before moving into a leadership role overseeing repair and replacement work. His responsibilities now include supervising projects, preparing estimates, and often serving as one of the first people customers meet when they contact the company.

That kind of employee longevity fits the broader story of a company that has transitioned across three generations without abandoning its family-business identity.

Packard's philosophy, according to the family, has remained centered on straightforward communication, quality materials, and workmanship the company is willing to stand behind. The company says many customers return when they move to another home or recommend Packard to younger generations of their own families.

## Looking toward another generation

More than five decades after the company was founded, Packard Roofing is operating in a Treasure Coast that looks very different from the one it entered in the 1990s.

Port St. Lucie has grown around it. PGA Village and surrounding communities have expanded. New homes continue to rise while existing roofs move through the repair and replacement cycle that comes with age and Florida weather.

The business has changed with that growth, but its leadership still describes Packard in distinctly family terms.

For Brian, continuing the company means carrying forward standards established by his grandfather and father rather than simply preserving a business name. He has described honesty, hard work and quality craftsmanship as values passed down through three generations.

Packard Roofing & Waterproofing provides roof repair, replacement, maintenance, and new-roof construction throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.
